title: Checkpoint: The Renaissance
objective: After this level you can explain what changed in art during the Renaissance and who led the change.
summary: Vasari called it a rinascita in 1550, but 'the Renaissance' as an era's name dates from 1855. The chapter's story, from the 1401 doors to the Sistine ceiling, in order.

cards.headline: Chapter 4 finale: did Leonardo know he lived in "the Renaissance"?
cards.body: Not by that name. First, the chapter's story in order. Then, who named the era, and when.

events.label: The dome rises with no centering

cards.headline: Vasari tells the story
cards.body: In 1550 Giorgio Vasari, a painter and architect who designed the Uffizi, published his Lives of the artists, revised in 1568. He told art's story in three acts: ancient greatness, medieval decline, then a rinascita, a rebirth, starting in 14th-century Tuscany and peaking with Michelangelo. It's seen as the first modern art history. Read it with care, though: he favored Tuscans and liked a good unverified anecdote.

mascot.line: The first art historian had favorites. Most of us do. It's why we check his stories.

cards.fact: "The Renaissance" as the name of an era dates only from 1855.
cards.context: Vasari's rinascita described a revival in art. Calling a whole period "the Renaissance" came three centuries later: the French historian Jules Michelet did it in 1855, and Jacob Burckhardt's influential book of 1860 spread it. The artists felt a rebirth. The capital R came afterwards.
